title: Can You Survive the Wreck?
author: Cut-Kooky
selftext:
Hey! I’d love to get some feedback on my game, **The Social Contract**. 

It’s a free, browser-based survival and exploration game where you wash up on a mysterious island after a ferry wreck. You explore, make decisions, interact with other survivors, and slowly uncover what’s really happening on the island.

It’s still in development, but I’ve put a lot of time into the story, choices, and gameplay. I’d really appreciate some honest feedback, especially on whether the opening hooks you and if the gameplay feels engaging.

You can play it here, no download needed: https://thesocialcontractgame.com/demo2/  
Thanks for doing this!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Cut-Kooky could you add more about how AI fit into your development process? Just mentioning that AI was used doesn't cut it. Under Rule 4, promotional posts need to contribute something by discussing how the game was actually made. Otherwise the sub gets buried in ads. If there's no update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: Cut-Kooky
replies.body:
Absolutely, that’s fair! I’m a solo developer working on The Social Contract, and AI has played a pretty significant role in bringing the game to life.  
I started with the overall concept, story, characters, and gameplay mechanics, then used AI to help turn those ideas into a playable browser-based game. A lot of the process has been back-and-forth: developing features, testing them, identifying what isn’t working, and using AI to help rewrite code, troubleshoot issues, and improve the experience.  
I’ve also used AI to help brainstorm dialogue, expand branching storylines, and experiment with different gameplay systems. The creative direction and decisions about what stays or gets changed are mine, but AI has made it possible to build something much more ambitious than I could have managed on my own.  
It’s definitely not a one-prompt-and-done project. There’s been a ton of trial and error, revisions, and rebuilding along the way. I’m still learning as I go, and that’s actually been one of the most interesting parts of the process.  
Happy to go into more detail about any particular aspect of development!

comments.author: channa92
comments.body:
some thoughts,   
1. add a copy-to-clipboard button for the save code; as a new player, I don't want to write it down  
2. there isn't a tun of into, I wasn't sure what I was supposed to do, but eventually I found my way to sleep, and then the crash happened.   
3. I couldn't figure out what to do after jumping into the sea, so I gave up.

I think the game has promise, but without some further tutorialization/guidance, it feels a bit tough to stick with.
